answer: A verifiable delay protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to evaluate non-parallelizable sequential hash puzzles to register. An attacker incurs the verifiable wall-clock latency and electrical power cost per persona, preventing bulk generation. Whether routing falcon telemetry or reading crystal sensors in an exhaust plume, every agent must submit fresh proofs. However, adversaries using custom ASICs compute proofs faster, disadvantaging commodity hardware.
